technique: From a straight-bar support facing away from the direction of lean used in standard straight-bar dips, perform controlled dips with high shoulder and wrist demand.
Only attempt with established straight-bar support strength.
setup: Advanced gymnastics-style variation; spot or mat as appropriate.
safety: Very high shoulder-extension and wrist stress — prefer parallel-bar and ring progressions; omit if unsure.
Limit depth; stop immediately with anterior shoulder pain (McKenzie et al. 2020).

evidenceRefs.label: McKenzie et al. 2020 — glenohumeral extension risk considerations in the dip
NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (technique/safety norms)
de Leva 1996 — adjusted segmental mass proportions (Zatsiorsky–Seluyanov)

bodyweightFraction.rationale: Feet free; almost all BM is supported through the upper limbs. Hands contact the bars (~1.2% BM per de Leva male hands), so estimate ~0.96–0.99. No published GRF %BM for dips found — estimate only.
